newsitem.title: PERU: SOCCER-SPORTING CRISTAL WINS PERU TITLE AFTER RULING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPORTING CRISTAL WINS PERU TITLE AFTER RULING.

text.p: Sporting Cristal became Peru's domestic soccer champions Saturday after a ruling awarded them the maximum three points from a match last week abandoned at 1-1 amid a players' brawl and crowd pitch invasion.
The "win" put Lima-based Sporting Cristal on an unassailable 64 points, ahead of nearest rivals Alianza Lima on 60 and Universitario on 57. All teams have one match remaining.

The decision by the Peruvian Football Federation's justice commission to give Sporting Cristal a nominal 2-0 victory over Universitario overturned a previous decision to award neither team any points from the match.

The game last Sunday dissolved into chaos at 1-1 in the second half after a controversial penalty decision in favour of Sporting Cristal had players attacking the referee and brought brawling fans pouring onto the pitch.
The referee needed a riot police escort to leave the field.

Saturday's ruling did not overturn the sanctions against Peruvian internationals and Universitario players Paolo Maldonado and Jose Carranza, who were suspended from playing for 90 and 60 days respectively for their part in the brawl.
Both players will miss Peru's November 10 World Cup qualifier against Venezuela.
